messages:
alex: FYI support escalated — Acme reports p99 for /v1/embeddings in eu-west jumped to ~2.4s around 18:12 UTC. They started seeing degraded UX. Support ticket #4521.

oncall-bot: ALERT: latency.p99 embeddings.eu-west > 2.0s (2.41s) — triggered 3m ago. Link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/latency-1819

maria: Thanks. Any recent deploys or model switches in eu-west?

jamal: No deploys to serving in eu-west in the last hour. I see a small spike in tail queuing on the GPU host pool (gpupool-eu-3). PID logs show transient KV cache misses.

leo: Can you paste p95/p99 timeseries?

jamal: pastebin: ```
p95: 0.88s -> 1.05s
p99: 0.92s -> 2.41s
requests/s: steady ~420 -> 430
queue depth: 4 -> 14
cpu util host: 79% -> 94%
kv-cache hit-rate: 98% -> 56%
```

alex: Oof kv-cache drop is suspicious. Possible cache eviction storm after a model rollout or bad prefix distribution. Any recent model version pinning changes?

maria: Checked model catalog — no version changes. But routing logs show a surge from customer token bucket for a few heavy batched requests (Acme's job-runner). They sent a large batch of 200 small texts (embedding unit) in parallel.

alex: That explains queue depth. We should run mitigation playbook: 1) apply per-customer rate limit to Acme, 2) enable circuit-breaker to fast-fail long tail requests, 3) if p99 persists, route eu-west traffic to eu-central or us-east fallback pool.

leo: I'll apply soft rate-limit at the API gateway for Acme (50r/s -> 20r/s) and add 429 backoff header. Applying now: `curl -X POST https://gw-admin/rate-limits -d '{"customer":"acme","limit":20}'`

jamal: On it — enabling CB for embeddings model on gpupool-eu: `deploy/cb enable --model embeddings-v2 --threshold 1.8s --window 120s`

oncall-bot: ACTION: rate-limit applied to customer=acme, limit=20r/s by leo at 18:15:22 UTC.

maria: Rolling in a fallback route in parallel — route 20% of eu-west traffic to eu-central using weighted routing so we don't overload fallback. Command: `routingctl set-weight embeddings eu-west->eu-central 0.2`

alex: Good. Also set quick KV-cache refresh: flush prefix cache for the hot prefix set  `cachectl flush --prefix acme-* --region eu-west` — but be careful with stampeding; we'll do staggered flush.

jamal: Flushed in 3 batches. Monitoring metrics now.

oncall-bot: METRICS: p99 eu-west embeddings now 1.45s (after rate-limit + CB + 20% failover). Queue depth down to 6. KV hit-rate 84%.

support-bot: Support ticket #4521 updated: actions taken: soft-rate-limit, circuit-breaker enabled, 20% fallback to eu-central. Customer notified with suggested retry/backoff.

alex: Short-term mitigation looks effective but not fully back to baseline. Next steps: 1) investigate why KV cache hit-rate dropped (eviction pattern), 2) add SLO guardrail config so future high-variance customers get automatic soft-limits, 3) create postmortem playbook entry.

maria: I'll open an infra ticket to capture eviction traces and heap growth for kv-store. Also adding a canary to detect large batch submissions from single tokens.

leo: I'll draft a small SLO guardrail RFC: automatic per-customer throttles if their 1m burst > X and p99 impact > Y for >=2m. Will link to runbook.

jamal: For immediate relief we should keep CB and rate-limit for another 30m and then gradually relax to monitor.

alex: Thanks team. I'll ping support later to confirm customer experience. Postmortem owner: maria. Follow-up checkpoint 19:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
